newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real falls 0.05 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real falls 0.05 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.05 percent to close at 1.0386 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank surprised the market by setting a weaker mini-band for the currency, dealers said.
"Everybody was expecting a new drop in the mini-band before the end of the year, but not today," one trader said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0385 and selling at 1.0435 reais in a morning auction.
The previous mini-band was set on Dec 19 between 1.0380 and 1.0430 reais to the dollar.

The Central Bank's move brought some doubts, dealers said. Before today, the market was expecting a total 0.6 percent drop in the mini-band during December. But with today's move, the Central Bank has already lowered the mini-band by 0.58 percent.
"Some dealers think the Central Bank will not do anything else this month. But others believe the Central Bank could lower the mini-band 0.05 percent once more before January," one dealer said.
On Tuesday, the forex market will be open only through noon and remain closed until Thursday.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.05 percent to end at 1.0442 to the dollar, following the drop in the mini-band.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.125 per greenback, up 0.44 percent, traders said.
